title: Eliminate Low Value
equation: Business Leverage = Value Created ÷ Complexity Carried
hook: Half the things in your business are only there because you already built them.
statement: If removing something wouldn't make your business less valuable, cut it, delay it, or simplify it.
explainer: Businesses hang onto stuff because someone asked for it once or cutting feels scary. But every extra piece adds upkeep, confusion, and decisions. Make each part prove it's worth the space.
sop: Pick one thing you're unsure about keeping.
Ask customers what would stop being valuable if you removed it.
Score Value Created and Complexity Carried from 1 to 10.
Remove, delay, or simplify anything that scores under 1.
Put the freed-up energy into what people actually care about.
equation_example: Value Created 4, Complexity Carried 8. 4 ÷ 8 = 0.5 Business Leverage. Under 1, so it's costing more than it's worth. Above 1 means it's earning its spot. Well below 1 means cut it, delay it, or simplify it.
question: Name one thing in your business you could remove tomorrow that nobody would actually miss.
closing_statement: Everything you keep should earn its complexity.
caption:
Principle Nº 243: Eliminate Low Value

Half the things in your business are only there because you already built them.

If removing something wouldn't make your business less valuable, cut it, delay it, or simplify it.

Your turn: Name one thing in your business you could remove tomorrow that nobody would actually miss.
